item.title: Inszone Insurance Acquires Pennsylvania Hospitality Specialist Progress Brokerage
item.description: Inszone Insurance Services, a national provider of commercial, personal, and benefits insurance, announced the acquisition of Progress Brokerage Group, LLC, a specialized insurance agency based in Springfield, Pennsylvania. Founded in 2013 by Ed Snow, Progress Brokerage Group has built a reputation serving bars, restaurants, taverns, and hospitality businesses throughout Pennsylvania and neighboring markets. “Their expertise in hospitality insurance and their dedication to client service make them an outstanding addition to Inszone as we continue expanding throughout the East Coast,” said Chris Walters, CEO of California-based Inszone Insurance Services.

item.title: Utica National Teams Up With NFL’s Buffalo Bills
item.description: Utica National Insurance Group announced a partnership with the National Football League’s Buffalo Bills. “We’re proud to stand alongside the Buffalo Bills and bring Bills’ energy to everything we do” State Kristen Martin, president and CEO of Utica National. As the football season approaches, Utica National said it will roll out a series of “campaigns and engagements designed to celebrate the partnership, energize fans, and reinforce its commitment to protecting what matters most.” The insurer is planning game day activations, co-branded community initiatives, and integrated marketing campaigns.

item.title: Making AI Work in Commercial Submission Intake
item.description: The industry no longer doubts whether AI benefits submission intake in commercial property and casualty (P&C) lines. Which parts of their submission intake workflow can realistically be automated? In this article, I'll share my perspective on where AI works best in submission intake today, why many initiatives never move beyond pilots, and what insurers should focus on if they want to launch submission intake AI over the next six to 12 months.

item.title: Curant.ai raises $3.1 million
item.description: Curant.ai has raised $3.1 million in seed funding to expand its AI platform for insurance operations. Curant integrates with insurers’ existing systems and provides source-backed insights and workflows configured around each carrier’s processes. Diagram led the round, with participation from Humania Insurance, Element Ventures, Blue Plains Capital and several angel investors.

item.title: Trucordia acquires the assets of Dominion Insurance Services
item.description: Trucordia has acquired the assets of Dominion Insurance Services , a California-based boutique brokerage specializing in lawyers professional liability and other professional liability lines. Founded in 1997 by Larry Hilton, and later joined by Wes Hilton, Dominion serves law firms and other professional clients, offering coverage including lawyers professional liability, fiduciary liability, patent agent liability, and insurance for accountants, architects and engineers. The acquisition expands Trucordia’s professional liability capabilities while providing Dominion with broader resources and operational support.

item.title: Utica National partners with the Buffalo Bills
item.description: Utica National has become an official home, auto and business insurance partner of the Buffalo Bills. The partnership will feature community-focused initiatives and events across Upstate New York, including the annual Utica National Kids Run and the Thanksgiving Blitz food drive in Buffalo. Utica National will also use the relationship to increase its brand visibility and promote its network of independent insurance agents.

item.title: AFBA Launches Benekiva Claims Platform
item.description: (Image source: AFBA.) Armed Forces Benefit Association (Alexandria, Va.) has gone live with Benekiva (West Des Moines, Iowa) for life insurance member-benefit claims processing. The AI-enabled claims platform was implemented in six months and supports AFBA’s benefit payment process from initial notification to reconciliation, according to an AFBA statement. The Benekiva deployment uses streamlined workflows and integrations to reduce double entry and speed claims processing, according to AFBA.

item.title: Verisk Acquires McKenzie Intelligence Services
item.description: (Image source: McKenzie Intelligence Services.) Verisk (Jersey City, N.J.) has acquired McKenzie Intelligence Services (London), a geospatial intelligence and event-response company focused on catastrophe and conflict event analysis. MIS provides rapid post-event damage assessment and real-time intelligence for major loss events, according to a Verisk statement. The acquisition brings MIS into Verisk’s Catastrophe and Risk Solutions business, adding geospatial event intelligence to Verisk’s catastrophe models, risk analytics and claims solutions.

item.title: Florida’s Fix for Insurance Crisis Puts More Risk on Homeowners
item.description: Florida changed how the legal system applies to insurance companies, making it more onerous for homeowners to use the courts to challenge denied claims or low payouts. Florida lawmakers knew they had a billion-dollar insurance problem. Scientists say this is a consequence of climate change, and a dynamic that will accelerate; many in the insurance industry say homeowners were weaponizing natural catastrophes to file fraudulent claims.

item.title: Cost of a Data Breach Reaches Record $5 Million on Average
item.description: Artificial intelligence has “radically shifted” the cyber risk landscape, and the average cost of a data breach has reached a record of nearly $5 million. AI-driven attacks increased 56% over last year’s study, adding about $1 million to the cost of a breach reach an average $4.99 million—a 12% increase. “Three quarters said they will deploy agents at higher rates in alert triage, vulnerability management, and scans and penetration testing.” IBM said average breach costs are worse in the U.S., reaching a record of about $11.5 million thanks to traditionally higher business costs and regulatory fines.

item.title: Workplaces Dialing Down ‘Tokenmaxxing’ as Focus Returns to ROI
item.description: A corporate fad of “tokenmaxxing” artificial intelligence is hitting its limits as workplaces using AI for everything are seeing costs rise without a spike in productivity. “Tokenmaxxing” refers to maximizing usage of tokens — the building blocks of generative AI that correspond to small pieces of text that an AI system reads or writes. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in May he was “excited to see what will happen with tokenmaxxing startups, both for how they work internally and the products they can build.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said, “If your $500K engineer isn’t burning $250K in tokens, something is wrong.” Facebook parent Meta had an internal competition rewarding token usage.

item.title: Cyclosporiasis Cases in Michigan Surpass 10,000 in Ongoing Outbreak
item.description: Michigan health officials reported 10,077 cases of cyclosporiasis on Wednesday, an increase of 397 cases since their last update a day earlier. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has received reports of 6,707 laboratory-confirmed domestic cases of cyclosporiasis, and said it was aware of more than 11,500 additional cases that are not laboratory confirmed or require further investigation across 45 states. Food and Drug Administration has linked the outbreak to iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants sourced from privately held Taylor Farms operations in central Mexico, but authorities are still looking for other potential sources given the size of the outbreak.

item.title: Dealer Installed Anti-Theft System Puts More Than 2M Vehicles in California at Higher Theft Risk
item.description: Computer scientists at the University of California, San Diego, uncovered a higher risk of theft in cars with dealer-installed anti-theft systems in Southern California since 2017. Vehicles purchased at Honda, Toyota, Mazda, Ford, and Jeep dealerships in Southern California from 2017 to present, with a sticker displaying the word “KARR” or “SWDS” on the driver’s-side window, are at risk. More than 2 million cars could be vulnerable to an attack that allows thieves to lock and unlock doors from as far as five yards away and immobilize vehicle engines remotely via a Bluetooth connection, according to a press release issued last week by the university.

item.title: Tokenized reinsurance securities will lower barriers and expand market access: HCI’s Patel
item.description: In light of HCI Group’s interest in taking risk on-chain and issuing tokenized reinsurance securities through a new partnership with Oxbridge Re, Chairman and CEO Paresh Patel has highlighted how tokenized reinsurance securities have the potential to expand access to the reinsurance market by lowering investment barriers and shortening investment duration. “While still in its early stages, we believe tokenized reinsurance securities have the potential to expand access to the reinsurance market by lowering investment barriers, shortening investment duration, and creating the potential for increased liquidity for qualified investors.” Back in June, Oxbridge Re and its subsidiary, SurancePlus, partnered with HCI Group to launch three Solana-based tokenized reinsurance securities tied to HCI’s recently formed reinsurer Fortex Re.

item.title: Swiss Re and SAS partner to strengthen insurers resilience through AI-driven risk intelligence
item.description: Global reinsurer Swiss Re and SAS, a global leader in data and AI, have entered into a partnership designed to help insurers strengthen resilience through AI-driven risk intelligence and advanced actuarial decisioning. As a member of the SAS Strategic Technology Partner Program, Swiss Re will now combine its CatNet natural catastrophe risk intelligence with SAS Insurance Life Cycle Accelerator, enabling insurers to incorporate predictive hazard insights directly into underwriting, pricing and portfolio management workflows. “The combination of SAS’ AI and actuarial modelling capabilities with Swiss Re’s catastrophe intelligence will enable insurers to make faster, more transparent and more resilient underwriting and pricing decisions.” Ali Shahkarami, Head Risk Data Solutions Insurance at Swiss Re, said, “Secondary perils are not secondary in terms of their financial impact.

item.title: Slide sees Q2’26 net income increase 92.4%, CoR improves to 57.6%
item.description: Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc., the technology-enabled insurer, has reported a net income of $134.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, up 92.4% compared to $70.1 million in the same period last year. For Q2 2026, Slide also reported a 47.9% increase in net premiums earned, to $360.6 million, with total revenue also increasing 47.9% to $386.8 million, compared to $243.9 million and $261.6 million, respectively, in the same period last year. According to the insurer, the increase was driven by growth of voluntary new business and renewals of previously acquired Citizens policies.

item.title: Lockton launches global Data Centres & Digital Infrastructure Practice
item.description: Lockton, an independent insurance broker, has announced the launch of its global Data Centres & Digital Infrastructure Practice, a consultative practice helping organisations navigate the risks associated with the infrastructure that stores, processes, and moves information. James Nelson will lead the Data Centres & Digital Infrastructure Practice in the US and Sam Baker in the UK, both partnering with Lockton leaders globally to drive the overarching strategy. Our practice is built to advise clients so they can navigate that complexity with confidence.” “The global data centre and digital infrastructure market is evolving at extraordinary speed,” said Chris Brown, CEO of Lockton International.

item.title: Relation Acquires Wisconsin’s Mid-State Insurance
item.description: Relation Insurance Services announced their acquisition of the assets of Mid-State Insurance. Founded in 1986 as an independent life and health agency in Milwaukee’s North Shore, Mid-State Insurance expanded its services to become a full-service, multi-line agency by 1989. Today, they are based in Mequon, Wisconsin, and offer a comprehensive suite of solutions including business and commercial insurance, employee benefits, and home, auto, life and health insurance, servicing clients throughout the Midwest and wherever their coverage needs exist nationally and internationally.

item.title: Brown & Brown Estimates Cost of Howden-Driven Talent War Could Hit $60M in 2026
item.description: Brown & Brown anticipates that the cost of the Howden-driven talent war for the full-year 2026 could hit $60 million – an increase from the $31 million it estimated last quarter . Andrew Watts, Brown & Brown’s chief financial officer and treasurer, who spoke during a recent analysts’ call to discuss Q2 2026 results. Brown & Brown, headquartered in Daytona Beach, Florida, previously had estimated that Howden’s US startup had poached close to 300 of its employees.

item.title: Verisk Buys McKenzie Intelligence Services, a UK-Based Catastrophe Analysis Firm
item.description: Verisk, the data analytics and technology firm, announced it has acquired UK-based McKenzie Intelligence Services (MIS), a geospatial intelligence and event response company that specializes in global real-time catastrophe and conflict event analysis. “By bringing MIS’s real-time geospatial intelligence together with Verisk’s catastrophe models, risk analytics, and claims solutions, we can give clients a more complete view of unfolding events so they can assess impacts, prioritize response and support policyholders more effectively.” MIS aggregates and analyzes multi-source geospatial data to provide re/insurers with rapid and precise insights to support: “We’ve worked with Verisk to integrate real-time event data for rapid accumulation analysis, so it felt like a natural fit to join the team, especially as catastrophes grow increasingly disruptive around the world,” said Forbes McKenzie, founder of MIS. Other MIS services include: “Verisk and MIS share a commitment to helping clients make faster, more confident decisions before, during, and after catastrophic events,” said Rob Newbold, president of Verisk Catastrophe and Risk Solutions, in a statement.

item.title: Soter Insure secures Series B funding to expand digital asset insurance platform
item.description: Soter Insure , a specialist provider of insurance products for the digital asset sector, has completed the first close of its Series B funding round , led by existing investor Galaxy Digital , with new backing from Coinbase Ventures and Franklin Templeton . Reaching the first close of our Series B – with Galaxy leading again and new partners like Coinbase Ventures and Franklin Templeton joining alongside the continued support of Brevan Howard Digital – is a powerful validation of the platform we are building.” Orser added that the funding would help accelerate product development, increase underwriting capacity and support the company’s international expansion. “Insurance remains a key gap to institutional adoption of digital assets, and Soter has built a platform that closes it.

item.title: Manger Insurance, Inc. Eliminates Manual Commission Reconciliation with Applied Recon
item.description: Applied Systems ® today announced that Manger Insurance, Inc., a North Dakota agency serving commercial, personal lines, and benefits clients with a heavy oil and gas book, has selected Applied Recon to eliminate the 2-3 days of manual commission reconciliation the agency previously spent every month. Eliminates Manual Commission Reconciliation with Applied Recon appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . Manger Insurance now relies on Applied Recon’s drag-and-drop statement matching, automatic policy number matching, and direct bill commission downloads, all natively embedded in Applied Epic, to close out commissions each month without manual data entry.

item.title: Terminal raises $20 million
item.description: Terminal, which provides a unified API for commercial trucking telematics data, closed a $20 million in Series A financing led by Battery Ventures, with participation from Intact Private Capital, Penske, Y Combinator, and Wayfinder Ventures. The round brings the company’s total funding to $26 million since its founding. Terminal works with insurance, fleet management, and logistics companies.

item.title: Tiptree to acquire Universal Shield Insurance Group
item.description: has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Universal Shield Insurance Group (“USIG”), a specialty property & casualty insurer operating in both admitted and excess & surplus markets. Tiptree will pay $100 million to acquire 100% of USIG while adding capital to help it grow. “USIG provides Tiptree with a new foundation in the specialty insurance sector and a clear path for scalable growth.

item.title: Zurich CEO Says Staff Let Go as Regulator Finma Imposes Partial Sales Ban
item.description: Zurich Insurance Group AG let go of more than 12 employees amid enforcement proceedings by the Swiss regulator Finma, Chief Executive Officer Mario Greco said. The regulator also imposed a sales ban on some policies in Zurich’s corporate life and pensions unit in Switzerland, Greco said in an interview Monday. The enforcement proceeding began after Swiss customers of the unit were sold policies — which are highly regulated — at lower prices than agreed upon with Finma, Greco said.

item.title: Johnson & Johnson Announces $5.5 Billion Settlement of Talc Lawsuits
item.description: Johnson & Johnson said on July 27 it would pay a n estimated $5.5 billion to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging its baby powder and other talc products cause ovarian cancer, in a landmark deal that could end a contentious legal battle that has dogged the company for a decade. J&J said the settlement covers about 76,000 claims, including ones consolidated in federal court in New Jersey, and related cases in state court, representing nearly all of the remaining talc claims against the company . Chris Seeger, an attorney who represents about 2,500 clients with talc claims and helped negotiate the agreement, said J&J could ultimately pay $7 billion or more.

item.title: Freehand Raises $75M Series B To Automate Fortune 500 Supply Chain Spend
item.description: Enterprise AI startup Freehand has raised $75 million in a Series B funding round to scale its autonomous AI agents, which manage complex supply chain spend and back-office operations for enterprise companies. “Instead of trying to catch them up to a technology paradigm that was sunsetting, we thought we could leapfrog them into a technology paradigm that was just rising.” While spend management platforms like Ramp focus on corporate cards, employee travel expenses, and bill payments, Freehand targets complex supply chain operations. Freehand’s fundraise also lands amid an uptick in venture funding to supply chain and logistics-related startups, with 2026 on pace to deliver the strongest year since 2022, per Crunchbase data , with $6.2 billion raised by such companies in the first half of this year across 350 deals.

item.title: The Sweet Science: Why The AI Era Belongs To Middleweights
item.description: Each year we speak with thousands of operators and founders, and one pattern is clear: The biggest long-term gains from AI will not flow to heavyweight incumbents or many AI-native startups but to scrappy middle-market technology companies, the middleweights. The next phase of AI disruption will be challenging, but middleweights can gain serious ground. Middleweights can win by making their software the system of record that AI calls into instead of software that AI replaces.

item.title: Exclusive: Former Meta And Slack Engineers Raise $15M For New Startup Centralize To Build A ‘Deal GPS’ For Enterprise Sales
item.description: Combined with a previous $4 million seed round led by Salesforce Ventures, Centralize has now raised $19 million since its 2023 inception to build what Kataria calls a “deal GPS” for enterprise revenue teams. “We missed the fact that the prior person had left, and the context had shifted hands, and no one had tracked that.” That breakdown planted the seed for Centralize, an enterprise sales platform emerging from stealth today alongside a $15 million Series A funding round led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA). The financing includes participation from Salesforce Ventures , 1 Y Combinator , 20 Sales , Ritual Capital, Adverb Ventures and high-profile angel investors including former Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield and Scott Woody , CEO and founder of Metronome .

item.title: Arch promotes Lynch to Head of ILS Experience and Operations
item.description: Arch Capital Group, the Bermuda headquartered insurance and reinsurance specialist, has promoted insurance-linked securities and retrocession operations specialist Bryan Lynch to the role of Head of ILS Experience and Operations. According to Lynch’s update on LinkedIn he actually stepped into the new role as Arch Capital’s Head of ILS Experience and Operations within its Arch Reinsurance division in April this year, after almost six years with the firm. Lynch joined Arch Capital Group in Bermuda in 2020, as Senior Operations Advisor, for ILS and retrocessions .

item.title: Japan quake impact on cat bonds, private ILS not expected to be material: Twelve Securis
item.description: Twelve Securis has reported that it does not expect any significant loss impact to the cat bond market from yesterday’s Kumamoto, Japan earthquake, while an assessment of its private ILS positions also does not suggest any material impact. Twelve Securis, the Zurich headquartered specialist catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities investment manager, is the latest to provide an event report related to the magnitude 6.8 earthquake that struck the Kumamoto prefecture of Kyushu, Japan yesterday. Twelve Securis stated in its report, “Based on the first estimates, the impact of the event is anticipated to be lower than, or similar to, the 2016 event after accounting for changes in property and values across Kyushu.” The ILS manager explained that a PERILS AG industry loss estimate for the 2016 earthquakes in Kumamoto was US $6.1 billion.

item.title: Verisk acquires McKenzie Intelligence Services to enhance catastrophe event insights
item.description: Verisk, a global data analytics and technology provider to the insurance industry, has acquired McKenzie Intelligence Services (MIS), a geospatial intelligence and event response company specialising in global real-time catastrophe and conflict event analysis. By acquiring MIS, Verisk enhances its leadership in Strikes, Riots and Civil Commotion (SRCC) and political violence risk analytics, bringing real-time, incident-level intelligence that activates when an event is unfolding. MIS offers both pre-event alerting and post-event exposure damage and quantification for catastrophic events, providing insurers, reinsurers, brokers and loss adjusters the intelligence to respond quickly.

item.title: Lemonade’s revenue jumps 79% to $294m in Q2’26
item.description: Lemonade, the AI-driven insurer, has reported second quarter 2026 revenue of $294.4 million, an increase of $130.3 million, or 79%, compared with Q2 2025. The company said the revenue growth was primarily driven by higher gross earned premium and an improved premium retention rate following the reduction in quota share cession rates that took effect in Q3 2025. Lemonade’s in-force premium (IFP), defined as the aggregate annualised premium for customers as of the period-end date, increased 32% in Q2 2026 to $1.43 billion.

item.title: Rokstone Agriculture expands livestock offering with new $20m AXA XL capacity agreement
item.description: Rokstone, an international specialty re/insurance managing general agent (MGA), has announced that its Agriculture division has entered into a new capacity agreement with AXA XL, introducing an excess livestock risks facility with limits of up to USD $20 million. Our tailored livestock risk solutions are going from strength to strength, thanks to top-tier capacity, market-leading talent, and ATOMX technology-empowered service.” Lorraine Mills, Underwriting Manager – Livestock, AXA XL, added: “We are pleased to partner with Rokstone Agriculture on this new excess livestock facility, which reflects our confidence in the team’s specialist underwriting expertise and disciplined approach to risk selection. The company said the facility strengthens its livestock proposition by providing additional capacity for excess livestock risks, while also offering an alternative source of capacity for primary livestock business written on a non-admitted basis.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis Consider Imposing Fees on Ships Sailing Through Red Sea: Sources
item.description: Yemen’s Houthi group is considering imposing fees on commercial ships sailing through the southern Red Sea, a week after declaring a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, regional sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The Houthis were looking into imposing fees on most traffic through the narrow Bab el-Mandeb gateway, which links the southern Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, the sources said. The objectives of such a move would be to normalize the practice of imposing fees on international waterways and increase pressure on the United States, the sources said.

item.title: Viewpoint: French Climate Lawsuit Offers Window Into Next Round of Global Legal Fight
item.description: The court’s ruling against TotalEnergies, under a French law passed in 2017, expands a growing front in the global legal fight against climate change . A recent decision by a French court requires a major European oil and gas company to report not only its own climate-warming emissions and those of its contractors but also those of its customers , who burn the oil and petroleum products the company sells. Read more: TotalEnergies Must Address Climate Risks Linked to its Products, French Court Rules TotalEnergies has said it will abide by the ruling , though it still may choose to appeal.

item.title: Markets/Coverages: CFC Brings Affirmative AI Cover to Media Companies; Lockton Launches Global Data Centers & Digital Infrastructure Practice
item.description: Lockton Launches Global Data Centers & Digital Infrastructure Practice Independent insurance brokerage Lockton said it launched a global data centers & digital infrastructure practice, a consultative practice helping organizations navigate the complex risks associated with the infrastructure that stores, processes, and moves information around the world. The specialty practice builds upon Lockton’s experience supporting complex digital infrastructure risks globally, including hyperscale campuses, multi-building developments, phased construction programs, operational portfolios, and power-related infrastructure. Alongside the media liability enhancements, CFC has also updated the policy’s cyber coverages with affirmative AI language.

item.title: Arch posts $1bn Q2 profit despite higher catastrophe losses
item.description: Arch Capital Group reported net income of $1 billion for the second quarter of 2026, as higher catastrophe losses weighed on earnings despite continued underwriting profitability and growth in investment income. “Clients not only come to us for capacity, but also for our underwriting expertise, claims capabilities, creative solutions and valuable perspectives that help them better manage risk.” Despite increased catastrophe losses and softer premium volumes, Arch maintained strong profitability in the second quarter, supported by disciplined underwriting, favourable reserve development and higher investment income as market conditions continue to normalize across insurance and reinsurance. Higher catastrophe losses were partly offset by  $165 million  of favourable prior-year reserve development, up from  $139 million  in the prior-year quarter.

item.title: INSTANDA partners with Diesta to streamline insurance payments and finance operations
item.description: The post INSTANDA partners with Diesta to streamline insurance payments and finance operations appeared first on Insurtech Insights . INSTANDA has entered a strategic partnership with insurance payments provider Diesta to help insurers, managing general agents (MGAs) and brokers simplify premium processing and strengthen finance operations. “Having Diesta’s advanced payments and finance operations capabilities embedded into INSTANDA’s offering is a major step towards our mission of enabling real-time payments across the insurance industry.” He added that the integration would help insurers, brokers and MGAs reduce operational risk, accelerate payment cycles and modernise insurance finance operations.

item.title: How Aspire General Turned an Early Technology Bet Into Claims Automation at Scale with Kyber
item.description: Media Contact Brett McKenzie Principal Strategist & Founder CoVerse Communications Brett@coversecomms.com 773-294-9724 The post How Aspire General Turned an Early Technology Bet Into Claims Automation at Scale with Kyber appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . NEW YORK and RANCHO CUCAMONGA, Calif., 7/28/2026 Kyber and Aspire General Insurance today released a new video case study exploring how an early partnership between a fast-growing regional carrier and a four-person startup evolved into a long-term collaboration that helped modernize claims operations, return valuable time to adjusters, and shape the growth of both organizations. Rather than selecting an established vendor, the company placed an early bet on Kyber, recognizing the opportunity to build with a team that could evolve its technology alongside Aspire’s business.

item.title: Soter Insure secures Series B funding
item.description: Soter Insure, a provider of specialized insurance products tailored to the digital asset economy, announced the first close of its Series B funding round, led by Galaxy Digital, who also led the Series A, with new participation from Coinbase Ventures and Franklin Templeton and follow-on investment from Brevan Howard Digital and other existing backers. The new funding will support the continued expansion of Soter Insure, deepening its underwriting and technology capabilities and scaling operations across key markets. Final close of the Series B will bring total funding to date of $23.5 million and over 500 BTC and 2000 ETH.

item.title: Hadron signs £500 million capacity deal with Integra Group
item.description: Hadron Insurance has partnered with Integra Insurance Solutions and Congregational to provide underwriting capacity for their UK home and church insurance programs. The four-year arrangement covers £500 million in gross written premium across the two MGAs, both of which form part of Integra Group. The depth of underwriting expertise, the purpose-built tech-led business model and the progressive approach to the delegated authority market make Hadron a fantastic partner for our long-term plans.” – Martin Cox, group CEO at Integra Group.

item.title: Mutuacat nombra a Leo Martínez director de Seguros
item.description: Mutuacat ha nombrado a Leo Martínez i Regales director de Seguros, asumiendo la responsabilidad ejecutiva sobre el negocio asegurador del grupo. Según la entidad, su labor se centrará en el crecimiento sostenible, la mejora del margen técnico y el refuerzo de la eficiencia operativa.

item.title: Brokers 88 se incorpora como asociada a Espabrok
item.description: Espabrok anuncia la incorporación de Brokers 88 a su estructura. Con presencia en todo el territorio nacional, la firma cuenta con oficinas en Barcelona, Madrid, Valencia y Bilbao.

item.title: Instagram, Facebook Ran AI ‘Nudify’ Ads from China, NGO Says
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s Facebook and Instagram have served thousands of ads for AI “nudify” apps in breach of the company’s policies, delivered by one of its few advertising partners in China, according to the nonprofit Tech Transparency Project. While Instagram and Facebook aren’t available in China, they’re attractive promotional tools for China-based businesses looking for a global audience. It singled out an app, created in China, that allows for the sharing of material some users have flagged as child pornography.
